title: Patience, again
hookLine: patience in obedience, patience from sin, patience in trials

cards: Three people, same morning. The first is getting out of a warm bed in the dark for the dawn prayer, and every part of her wants to stay.
The second is scrolling when a message arrives he knows he shouldn't answer the way he wants to. The third is in a hospital corridor, waiting for a door to open with news.
Teachers of the inward path would give all three the same name. Patience. Not one patience, they say, but three.

teach.b: In Arabic, patience is sabr. In Pickthall's translation, the Qur'an says: "O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast." Steadfastness is a good clue.
Sabr isn't sitting still; it's holding steady. Scholars of the inward path describe three kinds. Patience in obedience: keeping on with a good thing when it's hard, the woman getting out of bed.

teach.h: IN OBEDIENCE, FROM SIN, IN TRIALS.
teach.b: Patience from sin: holding back from a wrong thing when it's tempting, the man not hitting send. And patience in trials: staying steady when something hits you that you didn't choose, the person in the corridor.
A person can be strong in one and thin in another. Someone who never misses a prayer can still fire off the angry message. Someone calm in a crisis can still struggle with the alarm clock.
Then a moment in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet ﷺ passes a woman weeping at a grave and tells her to be patient. She doesn't recognize him and snaps that he hasn't been struck by what she has.
Later she learns who it was, and comes to his door to explain. He doesn't scold her.

teach.h: PATIENCE IS AT THE FIRST BLOW.
teach.b: He says, in effect, that patience is at the first blow. Not the weeping; the first moment.
This week's stations, good character, the Revival, turning back, watchfulness, the evening ledger, detachment, each need this one to last.
And if a loss ever feels too heavy to hold alone, you don't have to: in the US, call or text 988, any hour; elsewhere, local emergency help.

how: Muslims speak of sabr in three kinds: in keeping up acts of worship, in holding back from wrongdoing, and in bearing hardship; people often remind one another to have sabr in times of loss.

o: a calm temper that never gets angry about anything
sabr: holding steady in doing good, avoiding wrong, and trials
waiting quietly and doing nothing until things change

p: getting up for the dawn prayer

s: sabr means doing nothing and waiting
Pickthall puts it as steadfastness: holding steady, which is active.
in the hadith, patience is at the first blow
the Prophet ﷺ tells the weeping woman that patience counts at the first moment.
patience in Islam is only about bearing hardship
teachers describe three kinds: in obedience, from sin, and in trials.

games.q: a woman weeping at a grave snaps at a stranger who told her to be patient. later she learns it was the Prophet ﷺ and comes to explain. what does he say?
o: patience is at the first blow.
games.why: he doesn't scold her. he says patience is at the first blow: the first moment is where it counts.

practice: Hold up the three, keeping on with a good thing, holding back from a wrong one, staying steady in something hard, and ask which is thinnest in your life right now.

Picture the first moment it will be tested, the alarm, the reply, the waiting room, and picture yourself holding steady for just that moment. If you pray, you can rest on the line: Allah is with the steadfast.

wordCard.voice: Patience. Sabr: holding steady, in doing good, in holding back from wrong, and in what life brings. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: three patiences. Each of them begins with just the first moment. See you tomorrow.
